mcq_drop.why: vague 'current context' item with strawman distractors; not exam-style

patterns: APPSC asks single dates and facts: the UN Guidelines for Consumer Protection were first adopted in 1985, and the Drugs and Magic Remedies Act, 1954 bans objectionable advertisements.

UPSC-style statement items test consumer remedies: food samples can be tested, a legal heir can complain, fee exemption is not universal. Another tests District Forum composition (a woman member; more than one per state allowed).
Likely APPSC traps: 15 March vs 24 December, revised pecuniary slabs (₹50 lakh / ₹2 crore, from 2021), 45 vs 30-day appeals, CCPA date 24 July 2020.
The app goes deeper into the 2020/2026 e-commerce rules and CCPA penalties with multi-statement items. The facts are sound but the depth exceeds the PYQs.
